prompt:
Take the reference photograph of the hospital room and change ONE thing: the old man has moved. The camera, the room, the light and every object stay exactly as in the reference photograph, in the same places and the same sizes: the beds, the short raised grey side rail at the head end of the right-hand side of his bed, the grey handset hanging on the wooden foot board, the grey bag under the foot of the bed, the drip stand and its clear bag, the bedside cabinet and everything on it and on its shelf, the folded pale-green privacy screen, the empty second bed, the window and the trees, the wall clock, the wheelchair, the dispenser on the wall. His face, his white hair, his moustache, his pale-blue pyjama top, the clear oxygen tube under his nose and the white bands on his wrists stay exactly as in the reference photograph.

The old man now sits on the right-hand edge of his bed, as we look at it, halfway down the mattress, just below the short raised side rail, facing the right of the picture, his back half towards the window. The white duvet is pushed back onto the bed behind him. He wears long pale-blue pyjama trousers; his two feet stand flat on the grey floor in the pair of dark-blue felt slippers, which were standing beside the bed. With both hands he has taken hold of the two handles of the grey rollator walking frame, which stands in front of him on the floor exactly where it stood. His upper body is upright, his weight still on the mattress, caught at the instant before he stands up; he looks at the rollator with a determined, stubborn little smile.

The thin clear drip line still runs from the bag on the drip stand to the white dressing on his wrist, curving over the duvet. The white call button on its cable lies on the duvet behind him, out of his reach.

The whole picture carries no writing, numbers, print, symbol or logo anywhere, exactly as in the reference photograph.
